body:
## Feature Summary

Thank you to Ryan for the issue watcher and the standing coordinator, merged in #707. Could we make it clearer when a comment cancels an issue's approval, make that skip visible, or soften the rule now that the watcher is live?

## Problem Statement

This came out of checking the design for gaps in #761: https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/761.

After an issue is approved, the watcher stops accepting that approval for any of these changes made at or after the approval time:

- An edit to the issue body.
- A rename of the issue.
- A comment created or edited by a login other than the watcher's own login.

The watcher then skips the issue with the reason `edited_after_approval`. The test is `unchanged_since` in `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/predicates.py:275-297`. The exemption for the watcher's own login is `comment.author_login != own_login` at `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/predicates.py:292`. The coordinator and claim session use the same login as the watcher, so their comments do not cancel an approval.

The plan-approval code describes the repository as public in `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/stage_predicates.py:20-21`. Any other person, a bot, or a deleted account can therefore leave a comment that stalls an approved issue.

The skip is silent to the approver. `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/audit.py:71` classifies `edited_after_approval` as a skip with exit code 0. The local audit entry itself has kind `decision`, not kind `skip` (`src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/cycle.py:650-673,675-690`). Nothing is written to GitHub for this skip, and nothing tells the approver. The alert proposed in #717 W8 counts only cycles that exit with codes 3 to 7, so it would not cover this exit-0 skip.

To recover, someone has to clear the `Approved` field, wait a few seconds, and set it to `Yes` again as an approver (`docs/designs/issue-watcher-setup.md:566`).

This is a recorded choice, not a bug. The owner chose the rule. The design records accepted risk R17 in `docs/designs/issue-watcher-setup.md:566`, "anyone who can comment can cause that (risk R17)", and `docs/designs/issue-watcher-setup.md:645`, "Any commenter can stall an approved issue until it is approved again". The requirements file `.dev/releases/backlog/issue-watcher-zero-setup/requirements.md` records it in R19, where an issue edited after approval is refused and stays so, and R37, where an edit to the body, a comment or the title after approval still voids it.

We are not saying this was a mistake. Could the rule be softened now that the watcher is live? An approver can approve an issue, walk away, and return to find it never started, with no message anywhere they can see. A harmless "thanks", "+1", or bot notice is enough. The people best placed to notice cannot see the local audit log, so the cost lands on the approver and is invisible.

The file and line references were checked against `origin/master` on 2026-11-24. Line numbers can move as master moves.

## User Story

As an approver, I want to know when an approved issue has stopped and how to continue it, so that a harmless comment does not leave work waiting without my knowledge.

## Proposed Solution

Could the owner choose from these options and their order? None is decided.

- (a) Say it plainly. State in the issue template text and the runbook (`docs/designs/issue-watcher-setup.md`) exactly what cancels an approval. This is the cheapest option and changes no behavior.
- (b) Make the skip visible outside a local log. For example, add a line in watcher status output, a short issue comment such as "approval cancelled by a comment from X at time T, set Approved again to continue", or an alert. An issue comment would be a new GitHub write. Today the watcher does not make such writes, except for creating its trigger label during setup, so this needs the owner's agreement. It could share the alert destination chosen for #717 W8.
- (c) Make re-approval one step: one command, or the skill for the two human approvals, claim and plan, if the separate issue about that skill is filed. The approver would not have to clear and reset the field by hand.
- (d) Let only comments by approvers and the owner cancel an approval, not every commenter. Edits to the body and title would still cancel it.

These options are not exclusive. Options (a) and (b) fit together. Option (c) or (d) could follow.

Open questions:

1. Which of (a), (b), (c) and (d) should we do, and in what order?
2. Should the exemption for the watcher's own login stay as it is?
3. If a comment cancels an approval, who should be told, and where: a status line, issue comment, or alert?

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The owner records which options to take, their order, whether the own-login exemption stays, and who should be told where.
- [ ] If (a) is chosen, the issue template text and runbook plainly describe what cancels approval and how to approve again. Behavior stays unchanged.
- [ ] If (b) is chosen, an approver can see the skip and the recovery step in the agreed place without reading the local audit log. Any new GitHub write has the owner's agreement.
- [ ] If (c) is chosen, an approver can give a fresh approval in one step without manually clearing and resetting the field.
- [ ] If (d) is chosen, other commenters no longer cancel approval. Comments by the owner or approvers follow the agreed rule. Body and title edits still cancel approval.

## Out of Scope

- Changing the approval gate itself or who may approve. #722 covers the shared login.
- Replacing the merged watcher. The merged watcher is the design.

## Components Affected (from `/sc:analyze`)

The affected files depend on the option the owner picks:

- `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/predicates.py:275-297`: the existing `unchanged_since` check. Change it in place if comment eligibility changes.
- `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/audit.py:71,324-353` and `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/cycle.py:1014-1021`: the skip classification, decision record and skip path.
- `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/cycle.py:1400-1473` and `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/cli.py`: possible status output for (b). Status currently does not read the audit log, so exposing this skip needs an explicit design choice.
- `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/stage_predicates.py:7-10,17-22`: the separate plan-approval rules to review for (d), without changing who may approve.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` and `docs/designs/issue-watcher-setup.md:566,645`: template wording and runbook for (a), or documentation for other chosen options.
- `tests/issue_watch/test_predicates.py`, `test_cycle.py`, `test_audit.py`, `test_cli.py`, and `test_security_invariants.py`: approval timing, skip behavior, logging, status and limits on GitHub writes.
- `tests/issue_pipeline/test_complete.py:402-414`: regression coverage for the coordinator's own comments.


## Related Issues/PRs

- #707: the merged issue watcher and standing coordinator. This proposal builds on that work.
- #716, C8 note: the note says the plan's approval check already reads whether the body changed since approval through `unchanged_since`, and asks builders not to create a second competing "unchanged" test. Keep changes to the watcher's rule in `unchanged_since` itself. Current code distinguishes plan approval: `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/stage_predicates.py:7-10` says it deliberately does not reuse this watcher predicate because it skips host-login comments, including edited plan replies.
- #717: W2 says a plan written after approval voids approval, so a plan request must finish before the person approves. W8 proposes an alert after three bad cycles, which does not cover this skip.
- #722: the owner and AI helpers share one GitHub login. Comments by that login are exempt, which keeps the coordinator's own comments safe. It also matters for (d), because "comment by an approver" is only as precise as the login.
- #698: release-worker and plan-approval checks rest on text matching and an assignee shortcut. It covers who counts as an approver in the plan-approval code, which option (d) would reuse.
- #761: the gap check that found this, https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/761.
- #753: possible overlap from the lookup, "issue-watch: always accept maintainers and admins as approvers". Check its scope before taking option (d); it is not established as a duplicate.

## Priority

High: An approved issue silently stalls, so other work is blocked, the High trigger in the Priority rule set. (Clay)

## Fix approach

Repo: IronbellyOrg/IronClaude. Base branch: master.

Commands, in order: `/sc:workflow`, then `/sc:implement`, then `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3`.

Steps, in order:

- Step 1: Use `/sc:workflow` to record the owner's option choice and answers to the three open questions. The work depends on that choice. Assumption: this is an option-dependent plan, not approval to implement all four options.
- Step 2: For (a), update `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` text and `docs/designs/issue-watcher-setup.md`. For (b), plan the agreed output through `issue_watch/cycle.py`, `cli.py` and, if needed, `audit.py`. Account for `status_report` not reading the audit log today. A GitHub comment path needs the owner's agreement and review of the write restriction in `tests/issue_watch/test_security_invariants.py`, not an unreviewed write added to the read-only watcher.
- Step 3: For (c), identify the command or approval-skill entry point during workflow and preserve the approver check while issuing a fresh approval. For (d), review `issue_pipeline/stage_predicates.py` and the shared-login concern in #722 and #698, then change `issue_watch/predicates.py::unchanged_since` in place. Keep body and title checks. Set the own-login behavior only after the owner answers that question.
- Step 4: Use `/sc:implement` for only the agreed scope, update the matching watcher tests and runbook, then run the regression gate. Submit through `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3` against this repo and base branch.

## Test plan

- Tests to add or change depend on the owner's option choice. Assumption: apply only the relevant branches below; no new GitHub write is authorized by this plan.
- For (a), manually compare the issue template text and runbook with `unchanged_since`. Check body edits, title changes, comment creation and edits, equal timestamps, the own-login exception, and the recovery steps.
- For (b), extend `tests/issue_watch/test_cycle.py` and the agreed output tests in `test_cli.py` or `test_audit.py`. A harmless foreign comment should produce the agreed visible explanation and recovery step. Check repeated cycles and dry runs. If GitHub writes are agreed, review and test their limits in `test_security_invariants.py` using fake responses, not live writes.
- For (c), add tests at the chosen command or skill entry point for one-step recovery, an unauthorized caller, and recovery after the comment that invalidated approval. Keep the underlying approver checks.
- For (d), extend `tests/issue_watch/test_predicates.py` and the skip cases in `test_cycle.py` for owner, approver, other person, bot and missing author, with comments before, at and after approval and comments edited after approval. Retain the body and rename cases. Check the agreed own-login behavior against `tests/issue_pipeline/test_complete.py::test_the_coordinators_own_comment_leaves_unchanged_since_clean`.
- Focused gate: `uv run pytest tests/issue_watch/ tests/issue_pipeline/`.
- Regression gate: `uv run pytest`, `make lint`, and `make verify-sync`. If installed primitives change, edit their source of truth and run `make sync-dev` before `make verify-sync`.
- How a reviewer verifies: run the focused and regression gates, then inspect a fake-response case showing approval followed by a harmless foreign comment. Confirm the result matches the owner's chosen option, body and title edits still follow the agreed rule, and the documented recovery works. For (a) alone, confirm runtime behavior is unchanged. No live GitHub write is needed for this review.

## Backlog review, 2026-11-24

Read-only review of this issue against the current source and its history (automated analysis, then an independent evidence review that passed).

- **State:** still-relevant
- **Complexity / size:** Medium / M
- **Priority:** P2

#### Concrete next steps

1. Owner records the choice in chat: which of (a), (b), (c), (d), their order, whether the own-login exemption stays, and who is told where (the three open questions). The agent in that session records it; the owner writes no file.
2. If (a): add the plain wording of what cancels an approval and how to approve again to the issue template text (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml` and `other.yml` at minimum, UNVERIFIED which templates the owner wants) and keep the runbook lines 182, 566 and 645 in step. No behaviour change, no tests beyond a docs check.
3. If (b): decide the place (status line, issue comment, alert). A status line needs `status_report` to read the audit log. An issue comment is a new GitHub write and needs the owner's agreement. Add tests in `tests/issue_watch/test_cycle.py`, `test_cli.py` or `test_audit.py`.
4. If (c) or (d): resolve #722 (shared login) and #753 (approver rule) first; then change `unchanged_since` in place and extend `tests/issue_watch/test_predicates.py` and `test_cycle.py`.
5. Run `uv run pytest tests/issue_watch/ tests/issue_pipeline/`, `make lint`, `make verify-sync`; submit through `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3`.

#### Dependencies

- Needs: the owner's decision recorded (this issue's first acceptance criterion). For option (d): #722 (shared login, who approved) and #698 (who counts as an approver in plan approval); #753 (maintainers and admins as approvers) must be checked for overlap first.
- Option (b) shares an alert destination with #717 (W8).
- Blocks: nothing found.

#### Related issues

#707 (merged watcher; source of the rule), #761 (gap check that found this), #717 (W2 and W8; the W8 alert does not cover exit-0 skips), #716 (C8 note: keep one "unchanged" test), #722 (shared login), #698 (approver check by text and assignee), #753 (admins and maintainers as approvers; open, not a duplicate as far as read: its scope is who may approve, not what cancels approval).

#### Related PRs

#707 (merged; introduced `unchanged_since`, R17, R19, R37), #759 (merged; later watcher fix, unrelated to the rule), #729 (merged; records that the merged watcher is the design). No open PR addresses this issue.

_Limits: items marked UNVERIFIED in the text could not be checked in this read-only review. Nothing was changed on this issue other than this comment and its field values._

title: [FEATURE] A comment on an approved issue should not silently cancel the approval
